outcomes: In a Bazel repository, each Bazel package is a component, named by its label, and each changed file maps to the package that holds it
When the CI exported its graph with bazel query, the edges between packages come from it, so a change to a shared library marks the packages that use it as dependent
The JUnit logs of bazel test and the combined LCOV report of bazel coverage land on their packages, through the convenience links Bazel leaves at the repository root
nonGoals: Running bazel, or any query, build or test command: the CI writes the export, observe reads it
Components finer than a package: a target is not a component
Edges without an export: a BUILD file is Starlark, and observe does not evaluate it
Reading MODULE.bazel.lock or the external repositories' versions as dependency changes
Serving the detection from its own extension: the detector lives in @putnami/observe until the CLI can run a workspace probe outside a workspace
Packages whose BUILD file holds no rule, such as only exports_files: they are no component, and their files belong to the package above them, if any

requirements.text: A root that holds MODULE.bazel, WORKSPACE or WORKSPACE.bazel is a Bazel workspace. Its export is bazel-graph.json at the root, or the file --bazel-graph names, as bazel query 'deps(//...)' writes it with --output=streamed_jsonproto or jsonproto. Each directory with a BUILD or BUILD.bazel file and a rule of the main repository in the export is a component of source orchestrator and ecosystem bazel, named by its package label, // at the root.

Without an export, each directory with a BUILD or BUILD.bazel file, outside hidden, node_modules and root bazel-* directories and those .bazelignore or REPO.bazel ignore_directories names, is a manifest component without edges, unless another detector has a component at or above it; when it finds a package, the info observe.bazel_graph_missing names the export command. An export that does not parse or holds no main-repository rule is the warning observe.bazel_graph_unreadable, and the BUILD files answer.

A rule of one package that names a target of another package of the main repository among its rule inputs makes its package depend on the other. A label of the main repository is //pkg:name, @//pkg:name or @@//pkg:name. A target of an external repository, such as @maven//... or @@rules_go~//..., a package with no component, and the package itself are no edge.

Discovery follows the bazel-testlogs and bazel-out links of the root: the test.xml of each test target, shard or run under bazel-testlogs, and bazel-out/_coverage/_coverage_report.dat, are report candidates, recognized by content and named through the link. The cases of a log under bazel-testlogs/<package>/<target>/ go to the package of its test target, or the component enclosing it: the export rule that matches the directory, else the longest package that prefixes it. Each LCOV file goes to its package.

On a repository with //pricing, //api that depends on it, and //web: with the export, the three packages and the edge from api to pricing, and a change to pricing marks api dependent and web unaffected; without it, the three packages without edges and the info diagnostic; the bazel-testlogs cases and the combined LCOV land on their packages, with no unattributed case or unmapped file; a malformed export is a warning, never a failed run.
